environment_check.comparison_to_prior_runs: Identical to the configuration recorded on 2026-11-21, 2026-11-22, and 2026-11-23 (network.type=limited, allowed_hosts=[]). No change in four consecutive daily runs.

websearch_status.note: WebSearch tool (a separate backend not subject to the proxy host allowlist) remained usable, consistent with 2026-11-21/22/23. Used only for discovery of candidate leads per AGENTS.md; results are not claim-level evidence because no primary source was opened.

remediation_attempted_this_run.reason: On 2026-11-23, update_environment was called with the same required-hosts request and was refused by the tool itself with an explicit message stating that an unattended scheduled run has no person present to grant the approval the tool requires, and that the call should not be retried. Because this run is likewise an unattended scheduled fire (no live user input since the last genuine user message) and the underlying mechanism (a human-approval prompt) has not changed, update_environment and create_environment were not re-attempted this run. Re-attempting an approval-gated environment change from an unattended run would repeat an already-documented, architecturally certain refusal and waste the run's time without any chance of success.

conclusion: Fourth consecutive daily run blocked by the identical condition. All external HTTPS access via curl/WebFetch to research-relevant primary-source hosts (SEC, company IR sites, wire services) remains unavailable. This can only be resolved by a person adding hosts to the environment's Network access allowlist, or by running the routine interactively ("Run now") and approving an access-request prompt when shown. See reports/daily/2026-11-24.md for full detail and the escalation note.
